claim.why_it_matters: The PICTURE clause heading and its four subheadings are plain paragraphs rather than '## 5.9' / '### 5.9.y' headings like the sibling clauses; a heading-based section index misses the PICTURE clause.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 261 (VI-29) prints '5.9 THE PICTURE CLAUSE', '5.9.1 Function', '5.9.2 General Format', '5.9.3 Syntax Rules' and '5.9.4 General Rules' as section headings, in the same style as every other clause heading. In the transcription (page-261.md, and specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 11177) all five are plain paragraphs with no '#' markup, while the siblings carry heading markup: '# 5.8 THE OCCURS CLAUSE' and '## 5.8.1'-'## 5.8.3' / '### 5.8.4' (line 11069 onward), '### 5.9.5 Editing Rules' and '### 5.9.6 Precedence Rules' in the same clause, and '## 5.10 THE REDEFINES CLAUSE' with '### 5.10.x' (line 11481 onward). The heading text is present, so no prose is lost, but the document structure is wrong: a heading-based section index or citation lookup cannot find clause 5.9 or 5.9.1-5.9.4, and 5.9.5/5.9.6 appear to belong under 5.8. That is a genuine structural defect, not reflow or furniture.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate, with one detail corrected. The PDF prints 5.9 and 5.9.1-5.9.4 as headings, and the markdown renders all five as plain paragraphs. The siblings' heading levels are themselves inconsistent (# 5.8, ## 5.8.1, ### 5.8.4, ## 5.10, ### 5.10.x, ### 5.9.5), so the fix is to give 5.9 the clause level its siblings use and 5.9.1-5.9.4 the subclause level that 5.9.5 and 5.9.6 already have. It is not exactly '## 5.9' / '### 5.9.y' as the claim words it.
